words.meaning: may we two bear ill will

invocation.translation: Om. May He protect us both together. May He nourish us both together. May we work together with vigour. May what we study be full of light. May we never bear ill will towards each other. Om. Peace, peace, peace.
notes: The peace invocation of teacher and student, recited before and after the study of this Upaniṣad. It is not part of the DCS text; the wording is that of the edition of Śaṅkara's bhāṣya, which prints it at the opening and again after the last verse.
Śaṅkara's Kaṭha bhāṣya does not comment on this mantra.

sanskrit.deva:
उशन्ह वै वाजश्रवसः सर्ववेदसं ददौ ।
तस्य ह नचिकेता नाम पुत्र आस ॥ १ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
uśan ha vai vājaśravasaḥ sarvavedasaṃ dadau |
tasya ha naciketā nāma putra āsa || 1 ||

lines.iast: uśan ha vai vājaśravasaḥ sarvavedasaṃ dadau
lines.deva: उशन्ह वै वाजश्रवसः सर्ववेदसं ददौ

lines.iast: tasya ha naciketā nāma putra āsa
lines.deva: तस्य ह नचिकेता नाम पुत्र आस

padaccheda.iast: uśan ha vai vājaśravasaḥ sarvavedasam dadau tasya ha naciketāḥ nāma putraḥ āsa
padaccheda.deva: उशन् ह वै वाजश्रवसः सर्ववेदसम् ददौ तस्य ह नचिकेताः नाम पुत्रः आस

translations.text: Desiring its reward, Vājaśravasa, it is told, gave away all that he owned. He had a son named Naciketas.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the Upaniṣad, after saluting Yama and Naciketas: the word upaniṣad is from the root sad, ‘to shatter, to go, to loosen’, with upa and ni. It names the knowledge, because in seekers of liberation who have lost their thirst for things seen and heard of, and who approach it and dwell on it with firm resolve, it shatters ignorance and the rest, the seed of saṃsāra; or because it brings them to the supreme Brahman. The knowledge of the fire is also so called, because, leading to heaven, it loosens the host of troubles, lying in the womb, birth, old age, that return again and again. The book is called upaniṣad only in a secondary sense, as one says ‘ghee is life’. By this the one fit for the knowledge, its subject (the supreme Brahman that is the inner Self), its purpose (the final ending of saṃsāra, the attaining of Brahman) and their connection are stated.

Śaṅkara: uśan is ‘desiring’ the fruit of the Viśvajit sacrifice, in which all one's wealth is given away. vājaśravasaḥ is taken as a nominative, ‘the descendant of Vājaśravas’, a man whose fame (śravas) came from gifts of food (vāja). ha and vai recall an event of the past.

sanskrit.deva:
तं ह कुमारं सन्तं दक्षिणासु नीयमानासु श्रद्धाविवेश ।
सोऽमन्यत ॥ २ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
taṃ ha kumāraṃ santaṃ dakṣiṇāsu nīyamānāsu śraddhāviveśa |
so 'manyata || 2 ||

lines.iast: taṃ ha kumāraṃ santaṃ dakṣiṇāsu nīyamānāsu śraddhāviveśa
lines.deva: तं ह कुमारं सन्तं दक्षिणासु नीयमानासु श्रद्धाविवेश

lines.iast: so 'manyata
lines.deva: सोऽमन्यत

padaccheda.iast: tam ha kumāram santam dakṣiṇāsu nīyamānāsu śraddhā āviveśa saḥ amanyata
padaccheda.deva: तम् ह कुमारम् सन्तम् दक्षिणासु नीयमानासु श्रद्धा आविवेश सः अमन्यत

words.meaning: while they were being led away

translations.text: Though he was still a boy, faith entered him as the cows were being led away as gifts to the priests, and he thought:

notes: Śaṅkara: śraddhā is āstikya-buddhi, the conviction that what the scriptures teach is true, roused by the wish for his father's good. The dakṣiṇās are the cows being brought, in their portions, for the priests.

sanskrit.deva:
पीतोदका जग्धतृणा दुग्धदोहा निरिन्द्रियाः ।
अनन्दा नाम ते लोकास्तान्स गच्छति ता ददत् ॥ ३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
pītodakā jagdhatṛṇā dugdhadohā nirindriyāḥ |
anandā nāma te lokās tān sa gacchati tā dadat || 3 ||

lines.iast: pītodakā jagdhatṛṇā dugdhadohā nirindriyāḥ
lines.deva: पीतोदका जग्धतृणा दुग्धदोहा निरिन्द्रियाः

lines.iast: anandā nāma te lokās tān sa gacchati tā dadat
lines.deva: अनन्दा नाम ते लोकास्तान्स गच्छति ता ददत्

padaccheda.iast: pīta-udakāḥ jagdha-tṛṇāḥ dugdha-dohāḥ nirindriyāḥ anandāḥ nāma te lokāḥ tān saḥ gacchati tāḥ dadat
padaccheda.deva: पीत-उदकाः जग्ध-तृणाः दुग्ध-दोहाः निरिन्द्रियाः अनन्दाः नाम ते लोकाः तान् सः गच्छति ताः ददत्

translations.text: “Their water drunk, their grass eaten, their milk milked, their strength gone: joyless indeed are the worlds to which he goes who gives such cows.”

notes: Śaṅkara: nirindriyāḥ means no longer able to bear calves: old, barren cows.

sanskrit.deva:
स होवाच पितरं तत कस्मै मां दास्यसीति ।
द्वितीयं तृतीयम् ।
तं होवाच मृत्यवे त्वा ददामीति ॥ ४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
sa hovāca pitaraṃ tata kasmai māṃ dāsyasīti |
dvitīyaṃ tṛtīyam |
taṃ hovāca mṛtyave tvā dadāmīti || 4 ||

lines.iast: sa hovāca pitaraṃ tata kasmai māṃ dāsyasīti
lines.deva: स होवाच पितरं तत कस्मै मां दास्यसीति

lines.iast: dvitīyaṃ tṛtīyam
lines.deva: द्वितीयं तृतीयम्

lines.iast: taṃ hovāca mṛtyave tvā dadāmīti
lines.deva: तं होवाच मृत्यवे त्वा ददामीति

padaccheda.iast: saḥ ha uvāca pitaram tata kasmai mām dāsyasi iti dvitīyam tṛtīyam tam ha uvāca mṛtyave tvā dadāmi iti
padaccheda.deva: सः ह उवाच पितरम् तत कस्मै माम् दास्यसि इति द्वितीयम् तृतीयम् तम् ह उवाच मृत्यवे त्वा ददामि इति

translations.text: He said to his father, “Father, to whom will you give me?” He asked a second time and a third. The father said to him, “To Death I give you.”

notes: Śaṅkara: the boy offers himself so that the sacrifice may not fall short and bring harm to his father. Ignored at first, he asks again and again, and the father answers in anger.

sanskrit.deva:
बहूनामेमि प्रथमो बहूनामेमि मध्यमः ।
किं स्विद्यमस्य कर्तव्यं यन्मयाद्य करिष्यति ॥ ५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
bahūnām emi prathamo bahūnām emi madhyamaḥ |
kiṃ svid yamasya kartavyaṃ yan mayādya kariṣyati || 5 ||

lines.iast: bahūnām emi prathamo bahūnām emi madhyamaḥ
lines.deva: बहूनामेमि प्रथमो बहूनामेमि मध्यमः

lines.iast: kiṃ svid yamasya kartavyaṃ yan mayādya kariṣyati
lines.deva: किं स्विद्यमस्य कर्तव्यं यन्मयाद्य करिष्यति

padaccheda.iast: bahūnām emi prathamaḥ bahūnām emi madhyamaḥ kim svit yamasya kartavyam yat mayā adya kariṣyati
padaccheda.deva: बहूनाम् एमि प्रथमः बहूनाम् एमि मध्यमः किम् स्वित् यमस्य कर्तव्यम् यत् मया अद्य करिष्यति

translations.text: “Among many I go as the first, and among many as the middlemost. What purpose of Yama's is there that my father will accomplish through me today?”

notes: Śaṅkara: Naciketas reflects by himself. Among many sons or pupils his conduct is that of the best, or at least of the middling, never of the worst. His father spoke in anger and with no purpose in view; even so, his father's word must not prove false.

sanskrit.deva:
अनुपश्य यथा पूर्वे प्रतिपश्य तथापरे ।
सस्यमिव मर्त्यः पच्यते सस्यमिवाजायते पुनः ॥ ६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
anupaśya yathā pūrve pratipaśya tathāpare |
sasyam iva martyaḥ pacyate sasyam ivājāyate punaḥ || 6 ||

lines.iast: anupaśya yathā pūrve pratipaśya tathāpare
lines.deva: अनुपश्य यथा पूर्वे प्रतिपश्य तथापरे

lines.iast: sasyam iva martyaḥ pacyate sasyam ivājāyate punaḥ
lines.deva: सस्यमिव मर्त्यः पच्यते सस्यमिवाजायते पुनः

padaccheda.iast: anupaśya yathā pūrve pratipaśya tathā apare sasyam iva martyaḥ pacyate sasyam iva ājāyate punaḥ
padaccheda.deva: अनुपश्य यथा पूर्वे प्रतिपश्य तथा अपरे सस्यम् इव मर्त्यः पच्यते सस्यम् इव आजायते पुनः

translations.text: “Consider how those before us acted, and see how others act now. Like corn a mortal ripens, and like corn he is born again.”

notes: Śaṅkara: Naciketas says this to his father. Neither the forefathers nor good men now living have gone back on their word. Since man ripens and dies and is born again like corn, nothing in this passing world is gained by a falsehood: keep your word and send me to Yama.

sanskrit.deva:
वैश्वानरः प्रविशति अतिथिर्ब्राह्मणो गृहान् ।
तस्यैतां शान्तिं कुर्वन्ति हर वैवस्वतोदकम् ॥ ७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
vaiśvānaraḥ praviśati atithir brāhmaṇo gṛhān |
tasyaitāṃ śāntiṃ kurvanti hara vaivasvatodakam || 7 ||

lines.iast: vaiśvānaraḥ praviśati atithir brāhmaṇo gṛhān
lines.deva: वैश्वानरः प्रविशति अतिथिर्ब्राह्मणो गृहान्

lines.iast: tasyaitāṃ śāntiṃ kurvanti hara vaivasvatodakam
lines.deva: तस्यैतां शान्तिं कुर्वन्ति हर वैवस्वतोदकम्

padaccheda.iast: vaiśvānaraḥ praviśati atithiḥ brāhmaṇaḥ gṛhān tasya etām śāntim kurvanti hara vaivasvata udakam
padaccheda.deva: वैश्वानरः प्रविशति अतिथिः ब्राह्मणः गृहान् तस्य एताम् शान्तिम् कुर्वन्ति हर वैवस्वत उदकम्

translations.text: “A brahmin guest enters a house as fire itself, and people make this offering to appease him. Bring water, O son of Vivasvat!”

notes: Śaṅkara: sent by his father, Naciketas went to Yama's abode and stayed three nights while Yama was away. When Yama returned, his ministers or his wife said this to him. The appeasement is the offering of water for the feet, a seat and the like, which calms the guest as water calms a fire.

sanskrit.deva:
आशाप्रतीक्षे संगतं सूनृतां च इष्टापूर्ते पुत्रपशूंश्च सर्वान् ।
एतद्वृङ्क्ते पुरुषस्याल्पमेधसो यस्यानश्नन्वसति ब्राह्मणो गृहे ॥ ८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
āśāpratīkṣe saṃgataṃ sūnṛtāṃ ca iṣṭāpūrte putrapaśūṃś ca sarvān |
etad vṛṅkte puruṣasyālpamedhaso yasyānaśnan vasati brāhmaṇo gṛhe || 8 ||

lines.iast: āśāpratīkṣe saṃgataṃ sūnṛtāṃ ca iṣṭāpūrte putrapaśūṃś ca sarvān
lines.deva: आशाप्रतीक्षे संगतं सूनृतां च इष्टापूर्ते पुत्रपशूंश्च सर्वान्

lines.iast: etad vṛṅkte puruṣasyālpamedhaso yasyānaśnan vasati brāhmaṇo gṛhe
lines.deva: एतद्वृङ्क्ते पुरुषस्याल्पमेधसो यस्यानश्नन्वसति ब्राह्मणो गृहे

padaccheda.iast: āśā-pratīkṣe saṃgatam sūnṛtām ca iṣṭāpūrte putra-paśūn ca sarvān etat vṛṅkte puruṣasya alpamedhasaḥ yasya an-aśnan vasati brāhmaṇaḥ gṛhe
padaccheda.deva: आशा-प्रतीक्षे संगतम् सूनृताम् च इष्टापूर्ते पुत्र-पशून् च सर्वान् एतत् वृङ्क्ते पुरुषस्य अल्पमेधसः यस्य अन्-अश्नन् वसति ब्राह्मणः गृहे

words.meaning: sacrifices and works for the public good

translations.text: “Hope and expectation, the fruit of good company and of kindly speech, of sacrifices and of works for the public good, and all his sons and cattle: all this is destroyed for the man of little understanding in whose house a brahmin stays without food.”

notes: Śaṅkara: āśā is the wish for a desired thing not yet known to be within reach; pratīkṣā is the awaiting of one that is. saṃgata, sūnṛtā and iṣṭāpūrta stand for their fruits: what comes of keeping good company, of pleasant speech, of sacrifice, and of works such as the laying out of gardens.

sanskrit.deva:
तिस्रो रात्रीर्यदवात्सीर्गृहे मे अनश्नन्ब्रह्मन्नतिथिर्नमस्यः ।
नमस्तेऽस्तु ब्रह्मन्स्वस्ति मेऽस्तु तस्मात्प्रति त्रीन्वरान्वृणीष्व ॥ ९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tisro rātrīr yad avātsīr gṛhe me anaśnan brahmann atithir namasyaḥ |
namas te 'stu brahman svasti me 'stu tasmāt prati trīn varān vṛṇīṣva || 9 ||

lines.iast: tisro rātrīr yad avātsīr gṛhe me anaśnan brahmann atithir namasyaḥ
lines.deva: तिस्रो रात्रीर्यदवात्सीर्गृहे मे अनश्नन्ब्रह्मन्नतिथिर्नमस्यः

lines.iast: namas te 'stu brahman svasti me 'stu tasmāt prati trīn varān vṛṇīṣva
lines.deva: नमस्तेऽस्तु ब्रह्मन्स्वस्ति मेऽस्तु तस्मात्प्रति त्रीन्वरान्वृणीष्व

padaccheda.iast: tisraḥ rātrīḥ yat avātsīḥ gṛhe me an-aśnan brahman atithiḥ namasyaḥ namaḥ te astu brahman svasti me astu tasmāt prati trīn varān vṛṇīṣva
padaccheda.deva: तिस्रः रात्रीः यत् अवात्सीः गृहे मे अन्-अश्नन् ब्रह्मन् अतिथिः नमस्यः नमः ते अस्तु ब्रह्मन् स्वस्ति मे अस्तु तस्मात् प्रति त्रीन् वरान् वृणीष्व

translations.text: “Since you have stayed three nights in my house without food, O brahmin, a guest worthy of reverence, homage to you, O brahmin, and may it be well with me. Therefore choose three boons, one for each night.”

notes: Śaṅkara: Yama says this, approaching Naciketas with honour. prati: a boon in return for each night spent without food.

sanskrit.deva:
शान्तसङ्कल्पः सुमना यथा स्याद्वीतमन्युर्गौतमो माभि मृत्यो ।
त्वत्प्रसृष्टं माभिवदेत्प्रतीत एतत्त्रयाणां प्रथमं वरं वृणे ॥ १० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
śāntasaṅkalpaḥ sumanā yathā syād vītamanyur gautamo mābhi mṛtyo |
tvatprasṛṣṭaṃ mābhivadet pratīta etat trayāṇāṃ prathamaṃ varaṃ vṛṇe || 10 ||

lines.iast: śāntasaṅkalpaḥ sumanā yathā syād vītamanyur gautamo mābhi mṛtyo
lines.deva: शान्तसङ्कल्पः सुमना यथा स्याद्वीतमन्युर्गौतमो माभि मृत्यो

lines.iast: tvatprasṛṣṭaṃ mābhivadet pratīta etat trayāṇāṃ prathamaṃ varaṃ vṛṇe
lines.deva: त्वत्प्रसृष्टं माभिवदेत्प्रतीत एतत्त्रयाणां प्रथमं वरं वृणे

padaccheda.iast: śānta-saṅkalpaḥ su-manāḥ yathā syāt vīta-manyuḥ gautamaḥ mā abhi mṛtyo tvad-prasṛṣṭam mā abhivadet pratītaḥ etat trayāṇām prathamam varam vṛṇe
padaccheda.deva: शान्त-सङ्कल्पः सु-मनाः यथा स्यात् वीत-मन्युः गौतमः मा अभि मृत्यो त्वद्-प्रसृष्टम् मा अभिवदेत् प्रतीतः एतत् त्रयाणाम् प्रथमम् वरम् वृणे

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: “O Death, may Gautama, my father, be free of anxiety, glad at heart and without anger towards me; and when you send me back, may he recognise me and greet me. This I choose as the first of the three boons.”

notes: Śaṅkara: śāntasaṃkalpa: his anxious thought, ‘what will become of my son, gone to Yama?’, laid to rest. pratīta: with memory restored, recognising ‘this is my own son, come back’.

sanskrit.deva:
यथा पुरस्ताद्भविता प्रतीत औद्दालकिरारुणिर्मत्प्रसृष्टः ।
सुखं रात्रीः शयिता वीतमन्युस्त्वां ददृशिवान्मृत्युमुखात्प्रमुक्तम् ॥ ११ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yathā purastād bhavitā pratīta auddālakir āruṇir matprasṛṣṭaḥ |
sukhaṃ rātrīḥ śayitā vītamanyus tvāṃ dadṛśivān mṛtyumukhāt pramuktam || 11 ||

lines.iast: yathā purastād bhavitā pratīta auddālakir āruṇir matprasṛṣṭaḥ
lines.deva: यथा पुरस्ताद्भविता प्रतीत औद्दालकिरारुणिर्मत्प्रसृष्टः

lines.iast: sukhaṃ rātrīḥ śayitā vītamanyus tvāṃ dadṛśivān mṛtyumukhāt pramuktam
lines.deva: सुखं रात्रीः शयिता वीतमन्युस्त्वां ददृशिवान्मृत्युमुखात्प्रमुक्तम्

padaccheda.iast: yathā purastāt bhavitā pratītaḥ auddālakiḥ āruṇiḥ mad-prasṛṣṭaḥ sukham rātrīḥ śayitā vīta-manyuḥ tvām dadṛśivān mṛtyu-mukhāt pramuktam
padaccheda.deva: यथा पुरस्तात् भविता प्रतीतः औद्दालकिः आरुणिः मद्-प्रसृष्टः सुखम् रात्रीः शयिता वीत-मन्युः त्वाम् ददृशिवान् मृत्यु-मुखात् प्रमुक्तम्

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.
past passive participle m. acc. sg.

translations.text: “Auddālaki Āruṇi will recognise you and be towards you as he was before, by my leave. Free from anger, he will sleep happily through the nights, having seen you released from the jaws of Death.”

notes: Śaṅkara: Yama speaks. Auddālaki is Uddālaka himself, and Āruṇi ‘the son of Aruṇa’. matprasṛṣṭaḥ: ‘permitted by me’. yathā purastāt: with the same affection he had for you before.

sanskrit.deva:
स्वर्गे लोके न भयं किंचनास्ति न तत्र त्वं न जरया बिभेति ।
उभे तीर्त्वा अशनायापिपासे शोकातिगो मोदते स्वर्गलोके ॥ १२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
svarge loke na bhayaṃ kiṃcanāsti na tatra tvaṃ na jarayā bibheti |
ubhe tīrtvā aśanāyāpipāse śokātigo modate svargaloke || 12 ||

lines.iast: svarge loke na bhayaṃ kiṃcanāsti na tatra tvaṃ na jarayā bibheti
lines.deva: स्वर्गे लोके न भयं किंचनास्ति न तत्र त्वं न जरया बिभेति

lines.iast: ubhe tīrtvā aśanāyāpipāse śokātigo modate svargaloke
lines.deva: उभे तीर्त्वा अशनायापिपासे शोकातिगो मोदते स्वर्गलोके

padaccheda.iast: svarge loke na bhayam kiṃcana asti na tatra tvam na jarayā bibheti ubhe tīrtvā aśanāyā-pipāse śoka-atigaḥ modate svarga-loke
padaccheda.deva: स्वर्गे लोके न भयम् किंचन अस्ति न तत्र त्वम् न जरया बिभेति उभे तीर्त्वा अशनाया-पिपासे शोक-अतिगः मोदते स्वर्ग-लोके

translations.text: “In the world of heaven there is no fear at all. You are not there, and no one fears old age. Having crossed beyond both hunger and thirst, and gone beyond sorrow, one rejoices in the world of heaven.”

notes: Śaṅkara: Naciketas speaks. ‘You are not there’: Death does not suddenly prevail there, so no one, touched by old age, fears him as people do here. śoka is sorrow of the mind.

sanskrit.deva:
स त्वमग्निं स्वर्ग्यमध्येषि मृत्यो प्रब्रूहि तं श्रद्दधानाय मह्यम् ।
स्वर्गलोका अमृतत्वं भजन्त एतद्द्वितीयेन वृणे वरेण ॥ १३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
sa tvam agniṃ svargyam adhyeṣi mṛtyo prabrūhi taṃ śraddadhānāya mahyam |
svargalokā amṛtatvaṃ bhajanta etad dvitīyena vṛṇe vareṇa || 13 ||

lines.iast: sa tvam agniṃ svargyam adhyeṣi mṛtyo prabrūhi taṃ śraddadhānāya mahyam
lines.deva: स त्वमग्निं स्वर्ग्यमध्येषि मृत्यो प्रब्रूहि तं श्रद्दधानाय मह्यम्

lines.iast: svargalokā amṛtatvaṃ bhajanta etad dvitīyena vṛṇe vareṇa
lines.deva: स्वर्गलोका अमृतत्वं भजन्त एतद्द्वितीयेन वृणे वरेण

padaccheda.iast: saḥ tvam agnim svargyam adhyeṣi mṛtyo prabrūhi tam śraddadhānāya mahyam svarga-lokāḥ amṛta-tvam bhajante etat dvitīyena vṛṇe vareṇa
padaccheda.deva: सः त्वम् अग्निम् स्वर्ग्यम् अध्येषि मृत्यो प्रब्रूहि तम् श्रद्दधानाय मह्यम् स्वर्ग-लोकाः अमृत-त्वम् भजन्ते एतत् द्वितीयेन वृणे वरेण

translations.text: “You, O Death, know the fire that leads to heaven. Explain it to me, who have faith. Those whose world is heaven attain immortality. This I choose as my second boon.”

notes: Śaṅkara: adhyeṣi: ‘you remember, you know’. svargalokāḥ are the sacrificers who win heaven by building this fire. The immortality meant here is the deathlessness of the gods (devatva).

sanskrit.deva:
प्र ते ब्रवीमि तदु मे निबोध स्वर्ग्यमग्निं नचिकेतः प्रजानन् ।
अनन्तलोकाप्तिमथो प्रतिष्ठां विद्धि त्वमेतं निहितं गुहायाम् ॥ १४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
pra te bravīmi tad u me nibodha svargyam agniṃ naciketaḥ prajānan |
anantalokāptim atho pratiṣṭhāṃ viddhi tvam etaṃ nihitaṃ guhāyām || 14 ||

lines.iast: pra te bravīmi tad u me nibodha svargyam agniṃ naciketaḥ prajānan
lines.deva: प्र ते ब्रवीमि तदु मे निबोध स्वर्ग्यमग्निं नचिकेतः प्रजानन्

lines.iast: anantalokāptim atho pratiṣṭhāṃ viddhi tvam etaṃ nihitaṃ guhāyām
lines.deva: अनन्तलोकाप्तिमथो प्रतिष्ठां विद्धि त्वमेतं निहितं गुहायाम्

padaccheda.iast: pra te bravīmi tat u me nibodha svargyam agnim naciketaḥ prajānan ananta-loka-āptim atha u pratiṣṭhām viddhi tvam etam nihitam guhāyām
padaccheda.deva: प्र ते ब्रवीमि तत् उ मे निबोध स्वर्ग्यम् अग्निम् नचिकेतः प्रजानन् अनन्त-लोक-आप्तिम् अथ उ प्रतिष्ठाम् विद्धि त्वम् एतम् निहितम् गुहायाम्

words.meaning: the attaining of the endless world

grammar.en: past passive participle m. acc. sg.

translations.text: “I will explain it to you; learn it from me, O Naciketas, for I know well the fire that leads to heaven. Know this fire to be the means of attaining the endless world, and its support, lodged in the cave.”

notes: pra … bravīmi is one verb (prabravīmi), its parts separated in the verse.

Śaṅkara: Yama asks for attention so as to steady the pupil's mind, and then praises the fire. anantalokāpti: the means of gaining heaven. pratiṣṭhā: the support of the world, in its form as Virāṭ. ‘Lodged in the cave’: seated in the understanding of those who know.

sanskrit.deva:
लोकादिमग्निं तमुवाच तस्मै या इष्टका यावतीर्वा यथा वा ।
स चापि तत्प्रत्यवदद्यथोक्तमथास्य मृत्युः पुनराह तुष्टः ॥ १५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
lokādim agniṃ tam uvāca tasmai yā iṣṭakā yāvatīr vā yathā vā |
sa cāpi tat pratyavadad yathoktam athāsya mṛtyuḥ punar āha tuṣṭaḥ || 15 ||

lines.iast: lokādim agniṃ tam uvāca tasmai yā iṣṭakā yāvatīr vā yathā vā
lines.deva: लोकादिमग्निं तमुवाच तस्मै या इष्टका यावतीर्वा यथा वा

lines.iast: sa cāpi tat pratyavadad yathoktam athāsya mṛtyuḥ punar āha tuṣṭaḥ
lines.deva: स चापि तत्प्रत्यवदद्यथोक्तमथास्य मृत्युः पुनराह तुष्टः

padaccheda.iast: loka-ādim agnim tam uvāca tasmai yāḥ iṣṭakāḥ yāvatīḥ vā yathā vā saḥ ca api tat pratyavadat yathā uktam atha asya mṛtyuḥ punaḥ āha tuṣṭaḥ
padaccheda.deva: लोक-आदिम् अग्निम् तम् उवाच तस्मै याः इष्टकाः यावतीः वा यथा वा सः च अपि तत् प्रत्यवदत् यथा उक्तम् अथ अस्य मृत्युः पुनः आह तुष्टः

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. sg.
past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: Death told him of that fire, the beginning of the worlds: which bricks, how many, and how they are laid. And Naciketas repeated it just as it had been told. Then Death, pleased with him, spoke again.

notes: Śaṅkara: this verse is the Upaniṣad's own narration. lokādi: the first of the worlds, being the first to take a body. Pleased by the exact repetition, Death wishes to give a boon beyond the three.

sanskrit.deva:
तमब्रवीत्प्रीयमाणो महात्मा वरं तवेहाद्य ददामि भूयः ।
तवैव नाम्ना भवितायमग्निः सृङ्कां चेमामनेकरूपां गृहाण ॥ १६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tam abravīt prīyamāṇo mahātmā varaṃ tavehādya dadāmi bhūyaḥ |
tavaiva nāmnā bhavitāyam agniḥ sṛṅkāṃ cemām anekarūpāṃ gṛhāṇa || 16 ||

lines.iast: tam abravīt prīyamāṇo mahātmā varaṃ tavehādya dadāmi bhūyaḥ
lines.deva: तमब्रवीत्प्रीयमाणो महात्मा वरं तवेहाद्य ददामि भूयः

lines.iast: tavaiva nāmnā bhavitāyam agniḥ sṛṅkāṃ cemām anekarūpāṃ gṛhāṇa
lines.deva: तवैव नाम्ना भवितायमग्निः सृङ्कां चेमामनेकरूपां गृहाण

padaccheda.iast: tam abravīt prīyamāṇaḥ mahātmā varam tava iha adya dadāmi bhūyaḥ tava eva nāmnā bhavitā ayam agniḥ sṛṅkām ca imām aneka-rūpām gṛhāṇa
padaccheda.deva: तम् अब्रवीत् प्रीयमाणः महात्मा वरम् तव इह अद्य ददामि भूयः तव एव नाम्ना भविता अयम् अग्निः सृङ्काम् च इमाम् अनेक-रूपाम् गृहाण

translations.text: Pleased, the great-souled one said to him: “Here and now I give you one boon more. This fire will be known by your name alone. Accept, too, this chain of many forms.”

notes: Śaṅkara: this is a fourth boon, given out of delight at the pupil's fitness. sṛṅkā: a tinkling necklace of jewels; or else a course of ritual action that is not to be despised, that is, further knowledge of rites, which yields many results.

sanskrit.deva:
त्रिणाचिकेतस्त्रिभिरेत्य सन्धिं त्रिकर्मकृत्तरति जन्ममृत्यू ।
ब्रह्मजज्ञं देवमीड्यं विदित्वा निचाय्येमां शान्तिमत्यन्तमेति ॥ १७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
triṇāciketas tribhir etya sandhiṃ trikarmakṛt tarati janmamṛtyū |
brahmajajñaṃ devam īḍyaṃ viditvā nicāyyemāṃ śāntim atyantam eti || 17 ||

lines.iast: triṇāciketas tribhir etya sandhiṃ trikarmakṛt tarati janmamṛtyū
lines.deva: त्रिणाचिकेतस्त्रिभिरेत्य सन्धिं त्रिकर्मकृत्तरति जन्ममृत्यू

lines.iast: brahmajajñaṃ devam īḍyaṃ viditvā nicāyyemāṃ śāntim atyantam eti
lines.deva: ब्रह्मजज्ञं देवमीड्यं विदित्वा निचाय्येमां शान्तिमत्यन्तमेति

padaccheda.iast: triṇāciketaḥ tribhiḥ etya sandhim tri-karma-kṛt tarati janma-mṛtyū brahma-ja-jñam devam īḍyam viditvā nicāyya imām śāntim atyantam eti
padaccheda.deva: त्रिणाचिकेतः त्रिभिः एत्य सन्धिम् त्रि-कर्म-कृत् तरति जन्म-मृत्यू ब्रह्म-ज-ज्ञम् देवम् ईड्यम् विदित्वा निचाय्य इमाम् शान्तिम् अत्यन्तम् एति

words.meaning: one who has thrice built the Nāciketa fire

translations.text: “One who has thrice built the Nāciketa fire, who has attained union with the three and performs the three duties, crosses beyond birth and death. Knowing that shining one, all-knowing and born of Brahmā, worthy of praise, and realising him, one attains this peace completely.”

notes: Śaṅkara: ‘the three’ are mother, father and teacher, whose instruction he has duly received; or else the Veda, the smṛti and the conduct of the good; or perception, inference and scripture. The three duties are sacrifice, study and giving. brahmajajña is the all-knowing one born of Hiraṇyagarbha, the fire as Virāṭ. By knowledge and rites together he reaches the state of Virāṭ.
The DCS has the word brahmajajñam in its text but gives no analysis for it; the analysis here is ours.

sanskrit.deva:
त्रिणाचिकेतस्त्रयमेतद्विदित्वा य एवं विद्वांश्चिनुते नाचिकेतम् ।
स मृत्युपाशान्पुरतः प्रणोद्य शोकातिगो मोदते स्वर्गलोके ॥ १८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
triṇāciketas trayam etad viditvā ya evaṃ vidvāṃś cinute nāciketam |
sa mṛtyupāśān purataḥ praṇodya śokātigo modate svargaloke || 18 ||

lines.iast: triṇāciketas trayam etad viditvā ya evaṃ vidvāṃś cinute nāciketam
lines.deva: त्रिणाचिकेतस्त्रयमेतद्विदित्वा य एवं विद्वांश्चिनुते नाचिकेतम्

lines.iast: sa mṛtyupāśān purataḥ praṇodya śokātigo modate svargaloke
lines.deva: स मृत्युपाशान्पुरतः प्रणोद्य शोकातिगो मोदते स्वर्गलोके

padaccheda.iast: triṇāciketaḥ trayam etat viditvā yaḥ evam vidvān cinute nāciketam saḥ mṛtyu-pāśān purataḥ praṇodya śoka-atigaḥ modate svarga-loke
padaccheda.deva: त्रिणाचिकेतः त्रयम् एतत् विदित्वा यः एवम् विद्वान् चिनुते नाचिकेतम् सः मृत्यु-पाशान् पुरतः प्रणोद्य शोक-अतिगः मोदते स्वर्ग-लोके

words.meaning: one who has thrice built the Nāciketa fire

translations.text: “He who has thrice built the Nāciketa fire, having known this triad, and who, knowing thus, builds the Nāciketa fire, casts off the snares of death beforehand and, gone beyond sorrow, rejoices in the world of heaven.”

notes: Śaṅkara: the triad is the bricks, their number and the manner of laying them (verse 15). The snares of death are unrighteousness, ignorance, attachment, aversion and the like. purataḥ: even before the body falls. The heaven meant is the state of Virāṭ.

sanskrit.deva:
एष तेऽग्निर्नचिकेतः स्वर्ग्यो यमवृणीथा द्वितीयेन वरेण ।
एतमग्निं तवैव प्रवक्ष्यन्ति जनासस्तृतीयं वरं नचिकेतो वृणीष्व ॥ १९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
eṣa te 'gnir naciketaḥ svargyo yam avṛṇīthā dvitīyena vareṇa |
etam agniṃ tavaiva pravakṣyanti janāsas tṛtīyaṃ varaṃ naciketo vṛṇīṣva || 19 ||

lines.iast: eṣa te 'gnir naciketaḥ svargyo yam avṛṇīthā dvitīyena vareṇa
lines.deva: एष तेऽग्निर्नचिकेतः स्वर्ग्यो यमवृणीथा द्वितीयेन वरेण

lines.iast: etam agniṃ tavaiva pravakṣyanti janāsas tṛtīyaṃ varaṃ naciketo vṛṇīṣva
lines.deva: एतमग्निं तवैव प्रवक्ष्यन्ति जनासस्तृतीयं वरं नचिकेतो वृणीष्व

padaccheda.iast: eṣaḥ te agniḥ naciketaḥ svargyaḥ yam avṛṇīthāḥ dvitīyena vareṇa etam agnim tava eva pravakṣyanti janāsaḥ tṛtīyam varam naciketaḥ vṛṇīṣva
padaccheda.deva: एषः ते अग्निः नचिकेतः स्वर्ग्यः यम् अवृणीथाः द्वितीयेन वरेण एतम् अग्निम् तव एव प्रवक्ष्यन्ति जनासः तृतीयम् वरम् नचिकेतः वृणीष्व

translations.text: “This, O Naciketas, is the fire that leads to heaven, which you chose as your second boon. People will speak of this fire as yours alone. Choose the third boon, O Naciketas.”

notes: janāsaḥ is the Vedic nominative plural of jana.
Śaṅkara: this sums up what was given. Until the third boon is given, Yama remains in debt.

sanskrit.deva:
येयं प्रेते विचिकित्सा मनुष्ये अस्तीत्येके नायमस्तीति चैके ।
एतद्विद्यामनुशिष्टस्त्वयाहं वराणामेष वरस्तृतीयः ॥ २० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yeyaṃ prete vicikitsā manuṣye astīty eke nāyam astīti caike |
etad vidyām anuśiṣṭas tvayāhaṃ varāṇām eṣa varas tṛtīyaḥ || 20 ||

lines.iast: yeyaṃ prete vicikitsā manuṣye astīty eke nāyam astīti caike
lines.deva: येयं प्रेते विचिकित्सा मनुष्ये अस्तीत्येके नायमस्तीति चैके

lines.iast: etad vidyām anuśiṣṭas tvayāhaṃ varāṇām eṣa varas tṛtīyaḥ
lines.deva: एतद्विद्यामनुशिष्टस्त्वयाहं वराणामेष वरस्तृतीयः

padaccheda.iast: yā iyam prete vicikitsā manuṣye asti iti eke na ayam asti iti ca eke etat vidyām anuśiṣṭaḥ tvayā aham varāṇām eṣaḥ varaḥ tṛtīyaḥ
padaccheda.deva: या इयम् प्रेते विचिकित्सा मनुष्ये अस्ति इति एके न अयम् अस्ति इति च एके एतत् विद्याम् अनुशिष्टः त्वया अहम् वराणाम् एषः वरः तृतीयः

grammar.en: past passive participle m. loc. sg.
past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: “There is this doubt about a man who has departed: some say ‘he exists’, and others say ‘he does not’. Taught by you, may I come to know this. Of the boons, this is the third.”

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the third boon: what the two boons point to is all that the preceding mantra and brāhmaṇa, concerned with injunction and prohibition, can teach; it is not the true knowledge of the Self. The natural ignorance that superimposes action, its factors and its fruit on the Self is the seed of saṃsāra; to end it, the knowledge that Brahman and the Self are one, free of that superimposition and having the final good as its purpose, has to be taught. The story shows that even with the second boon one has not reached the end without knowledge of the Self.

Śaṅkara: ‘he exists’: some hold that there is a Self apart from body, senses, mind and intellect, which passes on to another body; others deny it. Neither perception nor inference can settle the matter, and the highest human end depends on knowing it.

अन्यं वरं नचिकेतो वृणीष्व मा मोपरोत्सीरति मा सृजैनम् ॥ २१ ॥

anyaṃ varaṃ naciketo vṛṇīṣva mā moparotsīr ati mā sṛjainam || 21 ||

lines.deva: देवैरत्रापि विचिकित्सितं पुरा न हि सुज्ञेयमणुरेष धर्मः

lines.iast: anyaṃ varaṃ naciketo vṛṇīṣva mā moparotsīr ati mā sṛjainam
lines.deva: अन्यं वरं नचिकेतो वृणीष्व मा मोपरोत्सीरति मा सृजैनम्

padaccheda.iast: devaiḥ atra api vicikitsitam purā na hi su-jñeyam aṇuḥ eṣaḥ dharmaḥ anyam varam naciketaḥ vṛṇīṣva mā mā uparotsīḥ ati mā sṛja enam
padaccheda.deva: देवैः अत्र अपि विचिकित्सितम् पुरा न हि सु-ज्ञेयम् अणुः एषः धर्मः अन्यम् वरम् नचिकेतः वृणीष्व मा मा उपरोत्सीः अति मा सृज एनम्

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. sg.

translations.text: “Even the gods had doubts about this in ancient times, for it is not easy to understand; subtle is this matter. Choose another boon, O Naciketas. Do not press me; release me from this one.”

notes: ati … sṛja is one verb (atisṛja), its parts separated in the verse.
Śaṅkara: the dharma spoken of is the thing called the Self. ‘Do not press me’: as a creditor presses his debtor.

sanskrit.deva:
देवैरत्रापि विचिकित्सितं किल त्वं च मृत्यो यन्न सुज्ञेयमात्थ ।
वक्ता चास्य त्वादृगन्यो न लभ्यो नान्यो वरस्तुल्य एतस्य कश्चित् ॥ २२ ॥

devair atrāpi vicikitsitaṃ kila tvaṃ ca mṛtyo yan na sujñeyam āttha |
vaktā cāsya tvādṛg anyo na labhyo nānyo varas tulya etasya kaścit || 22 ||

lines.deva: देवैरत्रापि विचिकित्सितं किल त्वं च मृत्यो यन्न सुज्ञेयमात्थ

lines.iast: vaktā cāsya tvādṛg anyo na labhyo nānyo varas tulya etasya kaścit
lines.deva: वक्ता चास्य त्वादृगन्यो न लभ्यो नान्यो वरस्तुल्य एतस्य कश्चित्

padaccheda.deva: देवैः अत्र अपि विचिकित्सितम् किल त्वम् च मृत्यो यत् न सु-ज्ञेयम् आत्थ वक्ता च अस्य त्वादृक् अन्यः न लभ्यः न अन्यः वरः तुल्यः एतस्य कश्चित्

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. sg.

translations.text: “Even the gods, indeed, had doubts about this, and you yourself, O Death, say that it is not easy to understand. No other teacher of it like you can be found, and no other boon at all is equal to this.”

notes: Śaṅkara: this boon leads to the highest good, while the fruit of every other is passing.

sanskrit.deva:
शतायुषः पुत्रपौत्रान्वृणीष्व बहून्पशून्हस्तिहिरण्यमश्वान् ।
भूमेर्महदायतनं वृणीष्व स्वयं च जीव शरदो यावदिच्छसि ॥ २३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
śatāyuṣaḥ putrapautrān vṛṇīṣva bahūn paśūn hastihiraṇyam aśvān |
bhūmer mahad āyatanaṃ vṛṇīṣva svayaṃ ca jīva śarado yāvad icchasi || 23 ||

lines.iast: śatāyuṣaḥ putrapautrān vṛṇīṣva bahūn paśūn hastihiraṇyam aśvān
lines.deva: शतायुषः पुत्रपौत्रान्वृणीष्व बहून्पशून्हस्तिहिरण्यमश्वान्

lines.iast: bhūmer mahad āyatanaṃ vṛṇīṣva svayaṃ ca jīva śarado yāvad icchasi
lines.deva: भूमेर्महदायतनं वृणीष्व स्वयं च जीव शरदो यावदिच्छसि

padaccheda.iast: śata-āyuṣaḥ putra-pautrān vṛṇīṣva bahūn paśūn hasti-hiraṇyam aśvān bhūmeḥ mahat āyatanam vṛṇīṣva svayam ca jīva śaradaḥ yāvat icchasi
padaccheda.deva: शत-आयुषः पुत्र-पौत्रान् वृणीष्व बहून् पशून् हस्ति-हिरण्यम् अश्वान् भूमेः महत् आयतनम् वृणीष्व स्वयम् च जीव शरदः यावत् इच्छसि

translations.text: “Choose sons and grandsons who will live a hundred years, many cattle, elephants and gold, and horses. Choose a vast domain of land, and yourself live as many years as you wish.”

notes: Śaṅkara: only one who has turned away from the impermanent sphere of rites and their results is fit for knowledge of the Self. Hence these offers, which tempt Naciketas with sons and the rest.

sanskrit.deva:
एतत्तुल्यं यदि मन्यसे वरं वृणीष्व वित्तं चिरजीविकां च ।
महाभूमौ नचिकेतस्त्वमेधि कामानां त्वा कामभाजं करोमि ॥ २४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
etat tulyaṃ yadi manyase varaṃ vṛṇīṣva vittaṃ cirajīvikāṃ ca |
mahābhūmau naciketas tvam edhi kāmānāṃ tvā kāmabhājaṃ karomi || 24 ||

lines.iast: etat tulyaṃ yadi manyase varaṃ vṛṇīṣva vittaṃ cirajīvikāṃ ca
lines.deva: एतत्तुल्यं यदि मन्यसे वरं वृणीष्व वित्तं चिरजीविकां च

lines.iast: mahābhūmau naciketas tvam edhi kāmānāṃ tvā kāmabhājaṃ karomi
lines.deva: महाभूमौ नचिकेतस्त्वमेधि कामानां त्वा कामभाजं करोमि

padaccheda.iast: etat tulyam yadi manyase varam vṛṇīṣva vittam cira-jīvikām ca mahā-bhūmau naciketaḥ tvam edhi kāmānām tvā kāma-bhājam karomi
padaccheda.deva: एतत् तुल्यम् यदि मन्यसे वरम् वृणीष्व वित्तम् चिर-जीविकाम् च महा-भूमौ नचिकेतः त्वम् एधि कामानाम् त्वा काम-भाजम् करोमि

translations.text: “If you think of any boon equal to this, choose it; choose wealth and long life as well. Be king, O Naciketas, over a great land. I will make you one who enjoys every desire.”

notes: Śaṅkara: edhi, ‘be’, means ‘be king’. The desires are both divine and human; Yama can grant them because his will does not fail.

sanskrit.deva:
ये ये कामा दुर्लभा मर्त्यलोके सर्वान्कामांश्छन्दतः प्रार्थयस्व ।
इमा रामाः सरथाः सतूर्या न हीदृशा लम्भनीया मनुष्यैः ।
आभिर्मत्प्रत्ताभिः परिचारयस्व नचिकेतो मरणं मानुप्राक्षीः ॥ २५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
ye ye kāmā durlabhā martyaloke sarvān kāmāṃś chandataḥ prārthayasva |
imā rāmāḥ sarathāḥ satūryā na hīdṛśā lambhanīyā manuṣyaiḥ |
ābhir matprattābhiḥ paricārayasva naciketo maraṇaṃ mānuprākṣīḥ || 25 ||

lines.iast: ye ye kāmā durlabhā martyaloke sarvān kāmāṃś chandataḥ prārthayasva
lines.deva: ये ये कामा दुर्लभा मर्त्यलोके सर्वान्कामांश्छन्दतः प्रार्थयस्व

lines.iast: imā rāmāḥ sarathāḥ satūryā na hīdṛśā lambhanīyā manuṣyaiḥ
lines.deva: इमा रामाः सरथाः सतूर्या न हीदृशा लम्भनीया मनुष्यैः

lines.iast: ābhir matprattābhiḥ paricārayasva naciketo maraṇaṃ mānuprākṣīḥ
lines.deva: आभिर्मत्प्रत्ताभिः परिचारयस्व नचिकेतो मरणं मानुप्राक्षीः

padaccheda.iast: ye ye kāmāḥ durlabhāḥ martya-loke sarvān kāmān chandataḥ prārthayasva imāḥ rāmāḥ sa-rathāḥ sa-tūryāḥ na hi īdṛśāḥ lambhanīyāḥ manuṣyaiḥ ābhiḥ mad-prattābhiḥ paricārayasva naciketaḥ maraṇam mā anuprākṣīḥ
padaccheda.deva: ये ये कामाः दुर्लभाः मर्त्य-लोके सर्वान् कामान् छन्दतः प्रार्थयस्व इमाः रामाः स-रथाः स-तूर्याः न हि ईदृशाः लम्भनीयाः मनुष्यैः आभिः मद्-प्रत्ताभिः परिचारयस्व नचिकेतः मरणम् मा अनुप्राक्षीः

translations.text: “Whatever desires are hard to obtain in the world of mortals, ask for them all as you please. Here are delightful women with chariots and musical instruments; such as these are not to be obtained by men. Have yourself served by them, given by me. But, O Naciketas, do not ask about death.”

notes: Śaṅkara: rāmāḥ are heavenly nymphs, so called because they delight (ramayanti) men. The question about death is whether or not one exists after dying.

sanskrit.deva:
श्वोभावा मर्त्यस्य यदन्तकैतत्सर्वेन्द्रियाणां जरयन्ति तेजः ।
अपि सर्वं जीवितमल्पमेव तवैव वाहास्तव नृत्यगीते ॥ २६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
śvobhāvā martyasya yad antakaitat sarvendriyāṇāṃ jarayanti tejaḥ |
api sarvaṃ jīvitam alpam eva tavaiva vāhās tava nṛtyagīte || 26 ||

lines.iast: śvobhāvā martyasya yad antakaitat sarvendriyāṇāṃ jarayanti tejaḥ
lines.deva: श्वोभावा मर्त्यस्य यदन्तकैतत्सर्वेन्द्रियाणां जरयन्ति तेजः

lines.iast: api sarvaṃ jīvitam alpam eva tavaiva vāhās tava nṛtyagīte
lines.deva: अपि सर्वं जीवितमल्पमेव तवैव वाहास्तव नृत्यगीते

padaccheda.iast: śvobhāvāḥ martyasya yat antaka etat sarva-indriyāṇām jarayanti tejaḥ api sarvam jīvitam alpam eva tava eva vāhāḥ tava nṛtya-gīte
padaccheda.deva: श्वोभावाः मर्त्यस्य यत् अन्तक एतत् सर्व-इन्द्रियाणाम् जरयन्ति तेजः अपि सर्वम् जीवितम् अल्पम् एव तव एव वाहाः तव नृत्य-गीते

translations.text: “These things last only till tomorrow, O Death, and they wear away the vigour of all a mortal's senses. Even a whole life is short indeed. Let the chariots be yours alone, and yours the dance and song.”

notes: Śaṅkara: śvobhāvāḥ: enjoyments of which it is doubtful whether they will be there tomorrow. They waste virtue, strength, understanding, vigour and good name. ‘A whole life’: even the lifespan of Brahmā is short.

sanskrit.deva:
न वित्तेन तर्पणीयो मनुष्यो लप्स्यामहे वित्तमद्राक्ष्म चेत्त्वा ।
जीविष्यामो यावदीशिष्यसि त्वं वरस्तु मे वरणीयः स एव ॥ २७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
na vittena tarpaṇīyo manuṣyo lapsyāmahe vittam adrākṣma cet tvā |
jīviṣyāmo yāvad īśiṣyasi tvaṃ varas tu me varaṇīyaḥ sa eva || 27 ||

lines.iast: na vittena tarpaṇīyo manuṣyo lapsyāmahe vittam adrākṣma cet tvā
lines.deva: न वित्तेन तर्पणीयो मनुष्यो लप्स्यामहे वित्तमद्राक्ष्म चेत्त्वा

lines.iast: jīviṣyāmo yāvad īśiṣyasi tvaṃ varas tu me varaṇīyaḥ sa eva
lines.deva: जीविष्यामो यावदीशिष्यसि त्वं वरस्तु मे वरणीयः स एव

padaccheda.iast: na vittena tarpaṇīyaḥ manuṣyaḥ lapsyāmahe vittam adrākṣma cet tvā jīviṣyāmaḥ yāvat īśiṣyasi tvam varaḥ tu me varaṇīyaḥ saḥ eva
padaccheda.deva: न वित्तेन तर्पणीयः मनुष्यः लप्स्यामहे वित्तम् अद्राक्ष्म चेत् त्वा जीविष्यामः यावत् ईशिष्यसि त्वम् वरः तु मे वरणीयः सः एव

translations.text: “A man is not to be satisfied by wealth. If we want wealth, we shall have it, now that we have seen you; and we shall live as long as you rule. But the boon I must choose is that one alone.”

notes: Śaṅkara: no gain of wealth has ever been seen to content anyone. ‘That one’: the knowledge of the Self.

sanskrit.deva:
अजीर्यताममृतानामुपेत्य जीर्यन्मर्त्यः क्वधःस्थः प्रजानन् ।
अभिध्यायन्वर्णरतिप्रमोदानतिदीर्घे जीविते को रमेत ॥ २८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
ajīryatām amṛtānām upetya jīryan martyaḥ kvadhaḥsthaḥ prajānan |
abhidhyāyan varṇaratipramodān atidīrghe jīvite ko rameta || 28 ||

lines.iast: ajīryatām amṛtānām upetya jīryan martyaḥ kvadhaḥsthaḥ prajānan
lines.deva: अजीर्यताममृतानामुपेत्य जीर्यन्मर्त्यः क्वधःस्थः प्रजानन्

lines.iast: abhidhyāyan varṇaratipramodān atidīrghe jīvite ko rameta
lines.deva: अभिध्यायन्वर्णरतिप्रमोदानतिदीर्घे जीविते को रमेत

padaccheda.iast: ajīryatām amṛtānām upetya jīryan martyaḥ ku-adhaḥsthaḥ prajānan abhidhyāyan varṇa-rati-pramodān ati-dīrghe jīvite kaḥ rameta
padaccheda.deva: अजीर्यताम् अमृतानाम् उपेत्य जीर्यन् मर्त्यः कु-अधःस्थः प्रजानन् अभिध्यायन् वर्ण-रति-प्रमोदान् अति-दीर्घे जीविते कः रमेत

words.meaning: the pleasures of beauty and love

translations.text: “Having come near the undecaying immortals, what decaying mortal who dwells on the earth below, and who knows of a higher goal, would delight in an over-long life, once he has reflected on the pleasures of beauty and love?”

notes: Śaṅkara: kvadhaḥsthaḥ: ku is the earth, which lies below the sky and the other worlds. He also records another reading, kva tadāsthaḥ, ‘how could he set his heart on such things?’. prajānan: knowing that a higher end is to be had from the immortals. The pleasures are seen, on reflection, to be unlasting.

sanskrit.deva:
यस्मिन्निदं विचिकित्सन्ति मृत्यो यत्साम्पराये महति ब्रूहि नस्तत् ।
योऽयं वरो गूढमनुप्रविष्टो नान्यं तस्मान्नचिकेता वृणीते ॥ २९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yasminn idaṃ vicikitsanti mṛtyo yat sāmparāye mahati brūhi nas tat |
yo 'yaṃ varo gūḍham anupraviṣṭo nānyaṃ tasmān naciketā vṛṇīte || 29 ||

lines.iast: yasminn idaṃ vicikitsanti mṛtyo yat sāmparāye mahati brūhi nas tat
lines.deva: यस्मिन्निदं विचिकित्सन्ति मृत्यो यत्साम्पराये महति ब्रूहि नस्तत्

lines.iast: yo 'yaṃ varo gūḍham anupraviṣṭo nānyaṃ tasmān naciketā vṛṇīte
lines.deva: योऽयं वरो गूढमनुप्रविष्टो नान्यं तस्मान्नचिकेता वृणीते

past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: “That about which they are in doubt, O Death, in the great matter of the passing beyond: tell us that.” This boon, which reaches into what is hidden: no other than this does Naciketas choose.

notes: Śaṅkara: sāmparāya is the world beyond; ‘great’, because a great end depends on it. gūḍham anupraviṣṭaḥ: the boon concerning the Self is deep and hard to discern. The last statement is the Upaniṣad's own.
